# apple_android_to_ios_app_mapping (Resource)

Links an Android app to this iOS app, so the App Store can recognize users moving from Android. Import it by ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "apple_android_to_ios_app_mapping" "example" {
  app_id       = data.apple_app.example.id
  package_name = "com.example.android"
  signing_certificate_sha256_fingerprints = [
    "14:6D:E9:83:C5:73:06:50:D8:EE:B9:95:2F:34:FC:64:16:A0:83:42:E6:1D:BE:A8:8A:04:96:B2:3F:CF:44:E5",
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `app_id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the app.
- `package_name` (String) Package name of the Android app, e.g. `com.example.app`.
- `signing_certificate_sha256_fingerprints` (List of String) SHA-256 fingerprints of the Android app's signing certificates.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the mapping.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = apple_android_to_ios_app_mapping.example
  identity = {
    id = "3c4d5e6f-7081-4293-a4b5-c6d7e8f90a1b"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) App Store Connect ID of the mapping.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import apple_android_to_ios_app_mapping.example 3c4d5e6f-7081-4293-a4b5-c6d7e8f90a1b
```
